title: Evaluation under a compatible coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $T$ be a conjunction of sign literals on the $n$ coordinates, with no coordinate appearing more than once. Let $\rho$ assign each coordinate either the status free, fixed to $1$, or fixed to $-1$, and let a completion of $\rho$ be any sign vector that agrees with its fixed coordinates and assigns arbitrary signs to its free coordinates. If some completion makes every literal of $T$ match its required sign, and no literal of $T$ lies at a free coordinate, then every completion of $\rho$ makes every literal of $T$ match its required sign.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a conjunction of literals with pairwise distinct coordinate indices
$\rho$ assigns each coordinate a free, fixed-$1$, or fixed-$(-1)$ restriction
There exists a Boolean input whose completion makes $T$ evaluate to $-1$
There are no literal positions of $T$ at free coordinates
The conclusion holds for every Boolean input used to complete $\rho$
